definitions.explanation: A place where four roads meet, forming a cross-shaped intersection. An older, more literary word compared to {交差点|こうさてん}.

examples.japanese: ⟦{古|ふる}い→古い：00488_furui⟧⟦{町並|まちな}み→町並み：10435_machinami⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{四|よ}つ{辻|つじ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧いくつ⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: There are many crossroads in the old townscape.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧{四|よ}つ{辻|つじ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{昔|むかし}→昔：01515_mukashi⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧や⟦{物|もの}→物：02259_mono⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{行|い}き{交|か}う→行き交う：14004_ikikau⟧{賑|にぎ}やかな⟦{場所|ばしょ}→場所：00829_basho⟧だった。
examples.english: This crossroads has been a lively place where people and goods have come and gone since long ago.

notes:
A compound of {四|よ}つ (four) and {辻|つじ} (intersection, street corner). {辻|つじ} is a kanji unique to Japanese (⟦{国字|こくじ}→国字：28106_kokuji⟧) that specifically means a road crossing.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {四|よ}つ{辻|つじ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{立|た}つ→立つ：00758_tatsu⟧: to stand at a crossroads
- {四|よ}つ{辻|つじ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{渡|わた}る→渡る：02441_wataru⟧: to cross the intersection

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{交差点|こうさてん}→交差点：01404_kousaten⟧: intersection — the standard modern term for any traffic intersection
- ⟦{十字路|じゅうじろ}→十字路：09387_juujiro⟧: crossroads — literally "cross-shaped road"; somewhat formal
- {辻|つじ}: street corner, intersection — the base word; often appears in place names
- {三叉路|さんさろ}: T-junction, three-way fork

CULTURAL NOTE:
{辻|つじ} and {四|よ}つ{辻|つじ} carry cultural significance in Japanese folklore. Crossroads were traditionally considered liminal spaces where the human and spirit worlds met. Many folk rituals ({辻占|つじうら} — divination at crossroads) took place at {四|よ}つ{辻|つじ}.
